anticipated_failure_modes: The answer alphabet has 9 values against query_chase's 24, and a running sum is a 1-D quantity, so latching may simply be easy enough here that the final-state readout succeeds. That would falsify T2 honestly and is the single most likely way this fails.
Removing attention removes the mechanism by which the earlier core became depth-limited, so all models may saturate and the comparison may be uninformative rather than negative.
If tau is not constructed carefully the crossing index may correlate with the answer value, which the shortcut audit is there to catch before anything is scored.
prediction.kill_condition: If T2 fails -- a final-state readout solves this family -- then the attribution result does NOT generalise and must be scoped to query_chase and chase_to_goal specifically. In that case no principle is claimed, the ATTRIBUTION-001 separation is reported as a property of associative-lookup tasks only, and this branch closes.
prediction.models: Six, sharing one streaming recurrent core with identical per-step inputs: fixed (final-state readout), fixed_supervised (final-state readout plus per-step predicate supervision), gated (explicit latch), mean_pooled (answer from the mean of all states), select (answer from the argmax-scored step, full depth), arrival (answer from the first step the predicate fires, with early stopping). Every model with a per-step head receives the per-step supervision.
prediction.pass_criterion: All three of T1, T2 and T3 hold.

predictions.T1_attribution_solves: select >= 0.95 AND arrival >= 0.95 answer accuracy, on every seed run.
predictions.T2_final_state_does_not: The better of fixed and fixed_supervised is at least 0.20 absolute BELOW select, on the mean over seeds.
predictions.T3_halting_is_free: arrival's answer accuracy is within 0.02 of select's, and arrival's mean step count gives a compute reduction of at least 1.5x against the full depth of 12.

prediction.protocol: AdamW 2e-3, 8 epochs, 500 batches of 128, grad-norm clip 1.0, normalised core, validation on 25 batches of 256 from a disjoint seed range. Identical for every model.
prediction.purpose: QNEURO3-ATTRIBUTION-001 measured, on one task family, that reading an answer from an input-selected step is what makes a first-match computation learnable, while a final-state readout fails even with matched supervision, an explicit latch, or 3x training. One family is one family. This opens a qualitatively different one, once.
prediction.seeds: 3 per model, fixed in advance as 0, 1, 2. No seed may be added after seeing results.

untouched_family.name: streaming_threshold_crossing
untouched_family.shortcut_audit_required_before_scoring: Report chance, the best accuracy obtainable from the crossing index alone, and the best accuracy from any position-independent statistic of the sequence. If any exceeds 0.30 the task is rebuilt before any model is scored, exactly as query_chase was after FAIL-026.
untouched_family.specification: A sequence of L = 12 tokens with values uniform on 1..9, and a threshold tau. The predicate fires at the first index k where the running sum of values reaches or exceeds tau. The answer is the VALUE of the token at index k, which is a 9-way classification and is statistically independent of k. tau is chosen per example so that the crossing index is uniform on 1..L.
why_qualitatively_different: Sequential streaming instead of graph traversal: one token per step, arriving in order.
Accumulate-and-compare instead of associative lookup. There is NO attention anywhere in the core, so the mechanism that carried query_chase is absent by construction.
The predicate is arithmetic (a running sum reaching a threshold), not an identity match.
The answer is a token VALUE, drawn from a small alphabet, not a node identity out of 24.
